 Cricket takes flight in the Falklands: ICC's smallest member with 3,800 population wins T20I series

 Print Photo credit: Falkland Islands Cricket Association/ ICC The Falkland Islands have hosted their first recognised international sporting event, with the territory's men's cricket team beating Costa Rica 6-2 in a T20I series at the Platinum Ground in Stanley, the capital. The series marked a first for cricket in the Falkland Islands and is also considered the first international sporting event held on the islands to be recognised by its international governing body, ICC said in a statement. Located off the mainland of South America, the Falkland Islands face several challenges when it comes to hosting international sport. There is only one commercial flight a week to and from the territory, connecting it with Santiago in Chile. The islands' tourist board has a “Getting Here” section on its website to help visitors plan their journeys. Some Antarctic expedition travellers stop there, while most visitors are on military assignments. The size of the population is another measure of how small the territory is. The Falkland Islands have around 3,800 residents, a number that could fit inside the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad, with about 128,000 seats still vacant. Even Saint Helena, the next-smallest ICC Member by population, has at least 1,000 more people. The Platinum Oval in Stanley is located further south than New Zealand's international grounds in Dunedin and Queenstown. It is also just over 1,000 kilometres from Antarctic land. Join conversation

 These factors leave a limited window for cricket to be played on the islands, particularly when it involves hosting an international series and bringing teams from overseas. Despite the challenges, the Falkland Islands managed to organise the series against Costa Rica. “For us to plan anything, we need a year plus or almost, and not just flights,” Falkland Islands captain, coach and secretary Cecil Alexander was quoted as saying by the ICC. “People have to take leave. You need to get the finances in order. And, Costa Rica was willing to work with us, holding this bilateral series.” “Working around something that's only once a week (a flight in and out of the country) makes it difficult." The two teams managed to play eight matches during their limited window, despite having to change the schedule midway through the series to account for bad weather and playing conditions.
